web.title: Set up Single Sign On
web.description: Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://support.whatfix.com/llms.txt · Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further
snippets: If you have published Whatfix content on your application, the End-user authentication feature prompts your end users to authenticate themselves with valid credentials using your organization’s Single Sign-on (SSO). For more information, see Set up End-User Authentication (opens in new tab). An Identity Provider (IdP) is an authority system that holds and verifies the user authentication information. Whatfix interacts with your IdP and trusts the information provided by the IdP to gain access to the application.
Whatfix supports login for content creators who use the Whatfix dashboard. SSO is an authentication process that enables users to access multiple applications with one set of login credentials.
The use of SSO significantly improves user experience by reducing password fatigue (not having to remember multiple passwords) and enhances security by limiting exposure to credential-based attacks.
Ensure the administrator configuring SSO is assigned to the Whatfix application in the Identity Provider (IdP) used for setup.
